prompt:
Primary request: Remix the existing completed shot to make its causal story unmistakably clear. Preserve the exact miniature CREATE SOMETHING Performance laboratory world, clear acrylic materials, near-black surface, hard raking light, black-and-white material treatment, single cobalt signal accent, tactile 12 fps replacement-animation stop-motion, 16:9 composition, and one uninterrupted shot. Change only the staging, choreography, camera direction, and narration described below.

Scene whole: Present one continuous left-to-right transparent channel with three physically connected stations: signal inlet, mechanical decision gate, and proof bay. In the first 1.25 seconds, hold a wider low three-quarter view that clearly shows the whole system and all three stations together. Nothing moves during this establishing hold. The viewer must understand the route before any action begins.

Element direction:
- The signal is one small matte cobalt isometric object. It must visibly travel from the far-left inlet, stop at the center gate, cross that same gate after approval, and arrive in the far-right proof bay. It must never duplicate, transform into a card, or remain behind in the left chamber.
- The decision gate is one near-black machined mechanism. It physically blocks the signal, performs exactly three distinct inspection ticks while the signal is completely still, then opens once. A very thin stop-red mechanical indicator may mark inspection; no glowing interface.
- The wake is one restrained optic-white stepped water trace. It begins only after the gate opens and follows directly behind the moving signal, physically connecting the approved passage.
- The proof receipt is one small optic-white physical card with a matching embossed cube mark and no legible writing. It remains hidden until the same cobalt signal enters the far-right proof bay, then ejects mechanically because the signal arrived.

Sequential timing: 0-1.25s establish the entire connected system, completely still. 1.25-3.25s only the cobalt signal travels from the inlet to the closed gate. 3.25-5.75s the signal stops; only the gate performs three inspection ticks and then opens. 5.75-8.5s the same signal crosses the gate and travels into the proof bay while one stepped white wake follows it. 8.5-10s the signal's arrival mechanically triggers the matching proof receipt and focus transfers to the receipt. 10-12s hold the completed scene absolutely still for trimming.

Camera: Keep one continuous 35mm-equivalent low three-quarter shot. Begin wider than the original so all three connected stations are readable. After 1.25 seconds, make one slow left-to-right lateral track that follows the same cobalt signal while always retaining the next station in frame. End with one restrained rack focus from the arrived signal to the issued receipt. No cut, no angle change, no handheld drift, no zoom jump.

Audio: Calm, precise editorial voiceover synchronized to the three causal beats. Three dry mechanical inspection ticks, one gate-release click, one restrained water-trace sound, and one tactile receipt-ejection click. No music.

Dialogue:
<dialogue>
- Narrator: "First, a signal. Then, a decision. Only then, action—and proof."
</dialogue>

Critical correction: The cobalt signal must visibly change location across the whole scene. Do not leave it in the left chamber while unrelated mechanisms animate elsewhere. The receipt must be visibly caused by that same signal entering the final proof bay; it must not appear independently.

Constraints: Preserve the original set, materials, palette, lighting, stop-motion cadence, and single-shot identity. Only one meaningful event moves at a time. No captions, subtitles, title card, logo, interface, fake evidence, legible text, people, duplicate signal, simultaneous unrelated motion, morphing objects, jump cuts, decorative science fiction, blue gradient, or copied Vox visual identity.
